AI panic sparks rare bipartisan moment on Capitol Hill
market.summary: Lawmakers who want to regulate AI are doing something unusual as Congress barrels towards a lengthy recess with no tangible solution in sight: They're working across the aisle. Why it matters: Bipartisanship is increasingly elusive on Capitol Hill of late, but it remains a crucial first step for action in a Senate that requires 60 votes to pass most legislation. The latest example: Sens. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) and Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) are pressing congressional leadership for a vote on their bill to establish a federal program to assess and monitor AI systems. "Recent incidents of rogue AI agent swarms hacking into public websites and systems have removed lingering doubts concerning the ability of these agents to wreak havoc on our cyber infrastructure," the pair wrote in a letter first obtained by Axios. "Congress cannot delay legislating to address frontier AI risks much longer. Industry-led evaluations are not enough." State of play: Several new bipartisan efforts to regulate AI have cropped up in the week since several current and former employees at Anthropic and OpenAI went public with concerns about the existential risks posed by their own products. Reps. Russell Fry (R-S.C.) and Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.) are founding a caucus focused on AI small businesses, called the Innovators Caucus, as Axios first reported Monday. Among the group's stated goals is starting work on a federal framework to regulate AI, as well as bringing small businesses to the AI policymaking table. The doomsday warnings have also breathed new life into existing bipartisan proposals to mitigate the dangers of AI. Rep. Ted Lieu (D-Calif.) has been publicly hawking his bill with Rep. Nathaniel Moran (R-Texas) to require AI companies to include a human-activated "kill switch" in their systems. Lieu has also privately pitched Democratic leadership on creating a bipartisan AI select committee if they retake control of the House next year. Reps. Lori Trahan (D-Mass.) and Jay Obernolte (R-Calif.) have also been championing their comprehensive AI regulation bill, the Frontier Act. Zoom out: It has been years since Congress passed multiple pieces of truly big bipartisan legislation, and decades since bipartisan lawmaking on marquee issues was a regular practice. The most common moments when cross-party cooperation sees a renaissance on Capitol Hill these days: crises. Consider what got passed in the 117th Congress, on the heels of the Jan. 6 attack and the COVID pandemic: $1.2 trillion in infrastructure spending , a $280 billion semiconductor and research bill and the first major gun safety law in decades, all with bipartisan majorities. Yes, but: House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) has signaled that his chamber will not take any action on the AI front before the House leaves for a six-week recess that doesn't end until after Election Day. Johnson said in a CNN interview Sunday that Congress should "not smother American innovation" with overly burdensome AI regulations. President Trump has gone even further in dismissing the urgency of federal AI regulations, writing in a Truth Social post Monday: "AI taking over the World, destroying Humanity, and all other things bad, is a HOAX." What to watch: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) has sounded a considerably more dire note on the issue. A potential House Democratic majority next year may be the place where AI regulation finally finds its footing on Capitol Hill.

CAPR.title: Capricor Therapeutics, Inc. Notice of September 28, 2026 Application Deadline for Class Action Lawsuit - Contact Lewis Kahn, Esq. at Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC, Before Application Deadline

CAPR.title: Kirby McInerney LLP Alerts Investors Who Acquired Capricor Therapeutics, Inc. CAPR Securities Between December 17, 2025 and July 26, 2026 of Pending Lawsuit

NVS.title: Immunotherapy Drugs Market 2026: Precision Medicine, Next-Generation Biologics and Expanding Cancer Indications Fuel Growth Opportunities
NVS.summary: The global immunotherapy drugs market is experiencing significant growth driven by advances in biotechnology, rising demand for targeted treatments, and expanding therapeutic applications across cancer, autoimmune, and inflammatory diseases. Key growth factors include increasing disease burden, robust drug pipelines, personalized medicine adoption, and combination therapy development. The Americas and Europe remain dominant markets, while Asia-Pacific is emerging as a high-growth region. Major pharmaceutical and biotech companies are increasing R&D investments and collaboration to accelerate innovation.

NVS.title: Oligonucleotide Therapeutics Market Outlook 2026-2035 - Featuring Profiles of Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Ionis Pharmaceuticals, and Sarepta Therapeutics
NVS.summary: The global oligonucleotide therapeutics market is projected to grow from USD 7.7 billion in 2025 to USD 72.1 billion by 2035, expanding at a 23.4% CAGR. Growth is driven by advances in RNA-based medicine, targeted delivery technologies, expanding applications beyond rare diseases into chronic and metabolic conditions, and increasing regulatory approvals. Antisense oligonucleotides lead the market at 39.9% share, while subcutaneous administration dominates at 56.4%. North America commands 57.9% market share.

NVS.title: Lupus Nephritis Market on a Growth Trajectory at a CAGR of 7% During the Forecast Period (2026–2036), as Innovative Therapies Gain Momentum | DelveInsight
NVS.summary: The lupus nephritis market is projected to grow at a 7% CAGR through 2036, driven by increasing disease awareness, improved diagnosis, and expanding adoption of targeted therapies. The market was valued at USD 2.1 billion in 2025 across seven major markets. Three therapies have received FDA approval (belimumab, voclosporin, and obinutuzumab), while a robust pipeline of innovative treatments including CAR-T therapies, complement inhibitors, and monoclonal antibodies is expected to transform disease management.

NVS.title: AZN's Etcamah Fails Late-Stage Study for First-line Breast Cancer

The drug was acquired through GSK's purchase of Nuvalent and is expected to support a supplemental FDA application for first-line use expansion.
